panel.summary: Webhook signature covers only the body — no timestamp/nonce, so a captured signed request can be replayed indefinitely
panel.evidence: `expected = sha256=HMAC(rawBody)` (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:53-55) binds nothing but the payload bytes: no `issuedAt` freshness window, no nonce cache, no binding to method/path. Anyone who observes one delivery (e.g. on the plaintext in-cluster hop documented in docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:69) can replay it forever. Impact is bounded because the only side effect is `touchUpdatedAt`, which is monotonic (document.service.ts:119-125) — a replay of an old event is a no-op and a replay of a recent one only re-sets the same value — so this is hardening, not an exploit. A freshness check on `body.attributes.issuedAt` (reject > N minutes old) would close it.
panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts::webhook signature covers only the body — no timestamp/nonce, so a captured signed request can be replayed indefinitely

coderabbit.summary: Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.
coderabbit.detail: **Consider using `findUniqueOrThrow` for the empty-data path instead of `prisma.document.update({ data: {} })`.** When `data` is empty, the current code calls `prisma.document.update({ data: {}, where })`. Prisma 6.6.0 may reject an empty `data` object at the client-validation level or generate invalid SQL (an `UPDATE` with no `SET` columns). The test mocks `prisma.document.update` so it wouldn't catch a real runtime failure. Returning the existing row via `findUniqueOrThrow` avoids the risk entirely and skips a needless write.
